chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from some of our companions, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the death came upon al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him), he said: 'O Qanbar! Look around — do you see from behind your door a believer from other than the progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him)?' He replied: 'God the Exalted, His Messenger, and the son of His Messenger know better than I.' He said: 'Call Muhammad ibn Ali for me.' So I (Qanbar) went to him, and when I entered upon him, he said: 'Has anything happened except good?' I said: 'Respond to Abu Muhammad.' So he hastened with his sandal strap without straightening it, and went out with me running. When he stood before him, he greeted. Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Sit down, for one such as you should not be absent from hearing a speech by which the dead are revived and the living can die. Be receptacles of knowledge and lanterns of guidance, for the light of the day — part of it is more luminous than other parts.

Do you not know that God made the children of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) Imams and gave distinction to some of them over others, and gave the Psalms to Dawud (peace be upon him)? And you know what He chose to distinguish Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with. O Muhammad ibn Ali! I fear envy for you, for God has described the disbelievers with it, and God Almighty said: [2:109] unbelievers, out of envy from themselves, even after the truth became clear to them. And God Almighty will not give Satan authority over you. O Muhammad ibn Ali! Shall I tell you what I heard from your father regarding you?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'I heard your father (peace be upon him) saying on the day of Basra: Whoever loves to honor me in this world and the next, let him honor Muhammad, my son.

O Muhammad ibn Ali! If I wished, I could have informed you while you were still a drop of seed in your father's loins! O Muhammad ibn Ali! Do you not know that al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), after my passing and the departure of my soul from my body, will be the Imam after me? And before God — Majestic is His Name — it is in the Book as an inheritance from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), which God Almighty has assigned to him in the inheritance of his father and his mother. God knew that you are the best of His creation, and He chose Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) from among you, and Muhammad chose Ali (peace be upon him), and Ali (peace be upon him) chose me for the Imamate, and I hereby choose al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'

Muhammad ibn Ali said to him: 'You are an Imam and you are my means to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). By God, I would have wished that my soul had departed before I heard this speech from you. Indeed, in my head there are words that neither can buckets drain nor can the songs of the winds alter — like a lexicon book in decorated pages. I intend to express them and find that I have been preceded to it — preceded by the Revealed Book or what the Messengers came with. It is a speech that exhausts the tongues of speakers and the hands of writers, until no pen is found and paper is brought as ashes, yet it cannot reach your virtues. And thus does God reward the doers of good, and there is no power except with God.

Al-Husayn is the most knowledgeable of us in knowledge, the most forbearing of us in clemency, and the closest of us to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) in kinship. He was a jurist before he was created, and he read the Revelation before he spoke. And had God known any goodness in anyone else, He would not have chosen Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). So when God chose Muhammad, and Muhammad chose Ali, and Ali chose you as Imam, and you chose al-Husayn — we submit and we are pleased. Who is there who would be pleased with other than him? And with whom other than him could we be safe from the difficulties of our affairs?'

key_terms.أَوْعِيَةَ الْعِلْمِ: Receptacles/vessels of knowledge — those who preserve and carry divine knowledge
key_terms.الْإِمَامَة: The Imamate — divine leadership of the Muslim community after the Prophet
key_terms.الْحَسَد: Envy — Imam Hasan warns Muhammad ibn Ali against this trait which characterized the disbelievers
key_terms.مَصَابِيحَ الْهُدَى: Lanterns of guidance — those who illuminate the path for others
key_terms.وِرَاثَة: Inheritance — used here in the theological sense of divinely ordained succession

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Hasan designate Imam Husayn as the next Imam before his death?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a momentous deathbed scene: Imam Hasan (AS), approaching death, summons his half-brother Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya (Muhammad ibn Ali) to formally designate Imam Husayn (AS) as the next Imam. The narrative unfolds in Medina, shortly before the death of Imam Hasan (AS) in 50 AH. The hadith establishes the principle of divine selection through a chain: God chose Muhammad, Muhammad chose Ali, Ali chose Hasan, and Hasan chose Husayn — a foundational doctrine in Shia theology of the Imamate. Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya's eloquent response acknowledges Husayn's unparalleled virtues, affirming his submission and acceptance.

Muhammad Bin Al Hassan and Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Suleyman Al Dalaymi, from some of our companions, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the death presented itself to Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Qanbar! Look around. Can you see from behind your door a Momin from other than the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>?’ So he said, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> are more knowing with it than I am’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Muhammad son of Ali<sup>asws</sup> for me’. 
So I (Qanbar) went over to him. So when I entered upon him, he said, ‘Has anything happened except good?’ I said, ‘Respond to (the call of) Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>!’ So he hastened upon wearing his shoes, and he did not even bother to even them, and went out with me running. So when he stood in front of him<sup>asws</sup>, he greeted. So Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Be seated, for it isn’t for the likes of you to be absent from hearing a speech the dead can be revived with and the living can be caused to die with. Become a retaining listener of the Knowledge and lanterns of Guidance, for the illumination of the day, part of it is more illuminating than (its other) part.

Do you not know that Allahazwj Made the children of Ibrahimas to be Imams and Merited some of them over the others, and Gave the Psalms to Dawoodas? And you know what Heazwj Preferred Muhammadsaww with. O Muhammad son of Aliasws! Iasws fear upon you of the envy, and rather Allahazwj has Described the Infidels with it, so Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Said [2:109] unbelievers after your faith, out of envy from themselves, (even) after the truth has become Manifest to them, and Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic will not Make for the Satanla an authority upon you. O Muhammad son of Aliasws! Shall Iasws inform you with what Iasws heard from your fatherasws with regards to you?’ He said, ‘Yes’. Heasws said: ‘Iasws heard your fatherasws saying on the day of Basra (Battle of the Camel): ‘The one who loved to be good to measws in the world and the Hereafter, so let him be good to Muhammad, myasws son’.

O Muhammad son of Ali<sup>asws</sup>! If you so desire, I<sup>asws</sup> can inform you (about yourself) while you were (a seed) in the forehead of your father!
O Muhammad son of Ali<sup>asws</sup>! Do you not know that Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>, after my<sup>asws</sup> passing away and the departure of my<sup>asws</sup> soul from my<sup>asws</sup> body, would be the Imam<sup>asws</sup> from after me<sup>asws</sup>, and in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Majestic is His<sup>azwj</sup> Name in the Book, as an inheritance from the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>? Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Chose it to be for him<sup>asws</sup> in the inheritance of his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> and his<sup>asws</sup> mother<sup>asws</sup>. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Knew that he<sup>asws</sup> is the best of His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures, there He<sup>azwj</sup> Chose Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> from you all, and Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> chose Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and Ali<sup>asws</sup> chose me<sup>asws</sup> with the Imamate, and I<sup>asws</sup> hereby choose Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>’.

So Muhammad son of Ali<sup>asws</sup> said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> are an Imam<sup>asws</sup>, and you<sup>asws</sup> are my Means to Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I would have loved myself to have gone (died) before I heard this speech from you<sup>asws</sup>. Indeed, and in my head there are (so many) words that neither can the buckets drain them nor can the songs of winds change them. These are like the book, the lexicon, in the decorated pages. I am thinking of initiating it, so I find that I have been preceded to it by the preceding Revealed Books or what the Rasools<sup>as</sup> came with. And it is a speech which exhausts the tongues from speaking with it and the hands to write these. I cannot find pens and these would turn the papers to ashes. Thus, one cannot reach to your<sup>asws</sup> merits, and that is how Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Recompenses the good doers, and there is no Strength except with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>.

Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> is our most knowledgeable one<sup>asws</sup>, and our heaviest one<sup>asws</sup> in forbearance, and our closest one<sup>asws</sup> from Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> in mercy. He<sup>asws</sup> was an understanding one before he<sup>asws</sup> was Created, and read the Revelation before he<sup>asws</sup> spoke, and had Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Known goodness in anyone (else) He<sup>azwj</sup> would not have Chosen Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>. So when Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Chose Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, and Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> chose Ali<sup>asws</sup> as an Imam<sup>asws</sup>, and you<sup>asws</sup> chose Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>. We submit and we are pleased. Who is he who would be please with other than him<sup>asws</sup>? And who, apart from him<sup>asws</sup>, can we be safe with from the difficulties of our affairs?’
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Muhammad have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami from one of our people from al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. (a.s.),

“When al-Hassan ibn Ali (a.s.) was about to leave this world he said, “O Qanbar, see if you there is any believer (in Islam) other than the members of the family of Muhammad (s.a.) behind the door.” He (Qanbar) said Allah, His Messenger and the grand son of His Messenger know better than I do.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Call to me Muhammad ibn Ali. I (Qanbar) then went to him and when I was in his presence he said, “I hope nothing but good has happened.” I said, “Answer the call of abu Muhammad. He quickly wore his shoes and did not even wear it properly. He came out with me running. When he arrived in the presence of al-Hassan (a.s.) he offered his greeting. Al-Hassan (a.s.) said to him, “Please, sit down. A person like you must not remain absent from hearing the words that can bring the dead to life and cause death to the living. You must be the container of knowledge and the beacon of guidance. Some of the lights of the day are brighter than others. Have you come to know that Allah made the sons of Abraham the Imams (‘A’imma) and granted to some of them more excellence than the others. He gave psalms to David and you know what kind of preference He granted to Muhammad (s.a.). O Muhammad ibn Ali, I fear for you of envy. Allah has said it to be of the characteristics of the unbelievers. Thus, Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has said, “. . out of envy, turn you back to disbelief, even after the Truth has become evident to them. .” [2:109]. Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has not given your control in the hands of Satan, O Muhammad ibn Ali. May I relate to you what I heard your father say about you?” He said, “Yes, I like to hear it.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “I heard your father say on the day of Basra, “Whoever likes to do good to me in this and the next life he should do good to my son, Muhammad.

O Muhammad ibn Ali if you would like I can inform you of the time you were only a potential person in the back of your father I can do so. O Muhammad ibn Ali, have you come to know that al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.) after I will die and my spirit depart my body will be the Imam (Leader with Divine Authority) afret me before Allah, Most great Whose name is, in the Book as the inheritance from the Holy Prophet. Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has added it to the inheritance from his father and mother. You are the choosen ones from His creatures. He selected Muhammad from among you and Muhammad (s.a.) selected Ali and Ali (a.s.) selected me for Imamat (Leadership with Divine Authority). I have choosen al-Husayn (a.s.) as the Imam (Leader with Divine Authority) after me.”

Muhammad ibn Ali then said, “ You are the my Imam (Leader with Divine Authority) and you are my connectio to Muhammad (s.a.). I swear by Allah, I wish I was dead before hearing these words from you. Certainly there is a great deal of facts in my head (about your excellence and virtues) that even with buckets can not be drained and by the songs of the winds can not be changee. It is like an encyclopedia with decorated pages. I ready myself to speak them out but I find others have preceded me like the preceding of a heavenly book or what the messengers have have brought. It is a book that exhausts the speaking tongue and the writing hand. I do not find enough pens to complete writing and it can turn all papers to ashes. Thus, there is no reach to your excellence and virtues. This is how Allah rewards those who do good and there is no power without Allah.

Al-Husayn (a.s.) is the most knowledgeable among us and his forebearance is the greatest among us in gravity. He is the closest to the Messenger of Allah among us in his relationship. He was a Faqih before he was created. He has read the messages of the Divine revelation before he would speak. Had Allah known any good in anyone He would not have choosen Muhammad (s.a.). Since Allah has choosen Muhammad (s.a.) and Muhammad (s.a.) choose Ali (a.s.) and Ali choose you as the Imam (Leader with Divine Authority ) and have choosen al-Husayn (a.s.) we accept and agree.
Who is he that accept a person other than him (al-Husayn (a.s.)) Who is he that would seek assistance in his difficulties from a person other than him (al-Husayn (a.s.) )?”
